construct:517d64db16ceb6e6a692.name: natural_recovery_propensity
construct:517d64db16ceb6e6a692.description:
Tendency for the original episode to remit or remain well without medication because of natural history, resilience, regression to the mean, and nonpharmacologic recovery.

Earlier measurement assessment: Only sparse retrospective evidence is available for the untreated illness course, so it remains scientific and identification context.

construct:6ca86c47aaf18b2472ce.name: internalizing_symptom_burden

construct:4cfc4a70f9d59a668364.name: past_escitalopram_response_tolerability
construct:4cfc4a70f9d59a668364.description:

Earlier measurement assessment: Historical response is represented by a sparse retrospective summary, so it remains measured assignment context rather than an executable dynamic state.

construct:4a7b8d4d0772b0b10e4e.name: duration_current_escitalopram_use

Has the medication actually been moving the needle, or did I just get better on my own — and what would my likely trajectory look like over the next two months if I taper off now versus stay on it?

construct:517d64db16ceb6e6a692.name: natural_recovery_propensity
construct:517d64db16ceb6e6a692.description:
Tendency for the original episode to remit or remain well without medication because of natural history, resilience, regression to the mean, and nonpharmacologic recovery.

Earlier measurement assessment: Only sparse retrospective evidence is available for the untreated illness course, so it remains scientific and identification context.

construct:6ca86c47aaf18b2472ce.name: internalizing_symptom_burden
construct:6ca86c47aaf18b2472ce.description: Primary outcome: latent depressive and anxiety symptom burden over the next two months, including mood, anhedonia, worry, irritability, somatic anxiety, and distress.

construct:4cfc4a70f9d59a668364.name: past_escitalopram_response_tolerability
construct:4cfc4a70f9d59a668364.description:
Historical symptom improvement, relapse prevention, side effects, and functional change while on escitalopram, reflecting drug effect plus natural recovery and expectancy.

Earlier measurement assessment: Historical response is represented by a sparse retrospective summary, so it remains measured assignment context rather than an executable dynamic state.

construct:4a7b8d4d0772b0b10e4e.name: duration_current_escitalopram_use
construct:4a7b8d4d0772b0b10e4e.description:
Length of continuous escitalopram use before taper decision, including time at stable maintenance dose.

Earlier measurement assessment: Historical exposure duration is observed only as sparse static context and feeds an unsupported neuroadaptation mechanism.

construct:47ab45d6fa00e93be7ee.name: patient_taper_preference_beliefs
construct:47ab45d6fa00e93be7ee.description:
Current motivation to taper or continue, perceived medication benefit, concerns about dependence or side effects, fear of relapse, and coping confidence.

Earlier measurement assessment: The sparse semantic proxy is entangled with the documented taper plan, so it remains assignment context rather than an executable latent state.

construct:7b3d7a5f98ae353c60b6.name: taper_speed_dose_reduction
construct:7b3d7a5f98ae353c60b6.description: Rate and size of escitalopram dose reductions, including abrupt, linear, hyperbolic, paused, or reversed taper patterns.

construct:b7418d1841c57d53abf8.name: adherence_to_regimen
construct:b7418d1841c57d53abf8.description: Consistency with intended dose or taper plan, including missed doses, extra doses, and reinstatement behavior.

construct:27f64faaddd59b2ad491.name: escitalopram_dose_taken
construct:27f64faaddd59b2ad491.description: Actual escitalopram amount ingested at each model tick after taper instructions and adherence are realized.

construct:2da513406663702e475d.name: withdrawal_symptom_burden
construct:2da513406663702e475d.description: Discontinuation symptoms after dose reduction, including dizziness, insomnia, anxiety, irritability, flu-like symptoms, nausea, and disequilibrium.

construct:eb28b45b275c6732596f.name: neuroadaptation_dependence_state
construct:eb28b45b275c6732596f.description:
Physiologic adaptation to sustained SSRI exposure that can make rapid reductions destabilizing even if the original disorder is inactive.

Earlier measurement assessment: The available text-derived adaptation proxy cannot independently resolve the physiologic state from duration and taper documentation.

construct:1ca8eec7961c69a0cbe1.name: stable_withdrawal_susceptibility
construct:1ca8eec7961c69a0cbe1.description: Stable person-specific susceptibility to SSRI discontinuation symptoms, distinct from the historical fact of prior withdrawal episodes.

construct:5bf588dc29d582cd7423.name: sleep_circadian_disruption
construct:5bf588dc29d582cd7423.description: Insomnia, hypersomnia, irregular sleep timing, circadian misalignment, and poor sleep quality.

construct:bb5a697c4e5f020f733d.name: perceived_stress_burden
construct:bb5a697c4e5f020f733d.description: Subjective stress load, threat appraisal, overload, uncontrollability, and daily hassles.

construct:ac82920bb78125ab0aca.name: external_stressful_events
construct:ac82920bb78125ab0aca.description: External shocks during follow-up such as loss, conflict, job strain, financial events, illness in others, or major schedule disruption.

construct:07f8d9915eaa311c9e50.name: physical_activity
construct:07f8d9915eaa311c9e50.description: Amount and regularity of movement and exercise sufficient to affect sleep, reward, energy, and mood regulation.

construct:ecfbf689dbd8add308bb.name: clinical_monitoring_rescue_care
construct:ecfbf689dbd8add308bb.description:
Frequency and quality of clinical follow-up, safety monitoring, medication review, dose rescue, and crisis support.

Earlier measurement assessment: Clinical contacts and rescue actions are sparse, event-triggered assignment signals that preserve treatment-change context without supporting a latent state.

construct:428de2b75c12e36ca19d.name: other_psychotropic_or_somatic_treatments
construct:428de2b75c12e36ca19d.description: Concurrent medication changes, supplements, sleep aids, anxiolytics, stimulants, hormonal treatments, or somatic treatments affecting symptoms or exposure.

extraction.how_to_measure: Inspect `clinical_note_text`, `assessment_text`, `journal_text`, `mood_valence`, `phq9_score`, and `gad7_score` for evidence that symptoms improved or remained well during periods without medication change, through nonpharmacologic coping, stable life conditions, or spontaneous remission. Rate as low, moderate, or high. Return null if the available evidence cannot distinguish natural recovery or resilience from medication response.

Use the `phq9_score` column directly when a PHQ-9 screening scale score is recorded. The score reflects depressive symptom burden over the prior two weeks ending at the visit date. Return null for support windows with no recorded PHQ-9 score.

Use the `gad7_score` column directly when a GAD-7 screening scale score is recorded. The score reflects anxiety symptom burden over the prior two weeks ending at the visit date. Return null for support windows with no recorded GAD-7 score.
Use the `mood_valence` column directly from Apple State of Mind entries. Average all observed entries within the day. Higher valence means better mood and therefore less internalizing symptom burden.

Within each day, inspect `local_date`, `journal_text`, `imessage_text`, `mood_labels`, and `mood_associations` for first-person evidence of depressed mood, anhedonia, anxiety, worry, irritability, panic, somatic anxiety, hopelessness, guilt, or distress. Rate severity as none, mild, moderate, or severe based only on evidence in that day. Return `none` only when there is usable mood-related text or labels and they indicate no such symptoms; return null when there is no usable symptom evidence in the support window.

Inspect `clinical_note_text`, `assessment_text`, `plan_text`, `journal_text`, medication fields, `phq9_score`, and `gad7_score` for historical improvement, relapse prevention, side effects, dose changes due to response/tolerability, or patient-reported benefit/harm while taking escitalopram. Rate net historical response/tolerability as poor_or_harmful, mixed_or_unclear, beneficial_with_side_effects, or clearly_beneficial_tolerated. Return null if no usable escitalopram response/tolerability history is available.

Use escitalopram-related `drug_name`, `medication_name`, `timestamp`, `local_date`, `days_supply`, `clinical_note_text`, and `plan_text` to estimate the length of continuous current escitalopram use before the taper decision. Prefer explicit duration statements in notes; otherwise use the span from first documented escitalopram record to the latest pre-taper escitalopram record when continuity is plausible from fills/notes. Return duration in days; return null if current-use duration cannot be estimated.

Within each day, inspect `journal_text`, `imessage_text`, `clinical_note_text`, and `plan_text` for the patient's motivation to taper or continue escitalopram, perceived benefit, side-effect concerns, dependence concerns, fear of relapse, and coping confidence. Rate taper preference as wants_continue, ambivalent, prefers_slow_taper, or wants_stop_or_fast_taper. Return null if there is no usable preference/belief evidence.

Within each day, inspect `plan_text`, `clinical_note_text`, `medication_action`, `medication_name`, and `drug_name` for the escitalopram taper plan. Classify the intended reduction speed as none_or_continue, slow_or_paused_reduction, moderate_reduction, or rapid_stop_or_large_reduction. Return null if no escitalopram taper or continuation plan is documented in the support window.

Within each day, inspect `clinical_note_text`, `plan_text`, `journal_text`, and `imessage_text` for evidence about taking escitalopram as prescribed, missed doses, extra doses, self-directed changes, or reinstatement. Rate adherence as poor, partial, or consistent. Use `consistent` only when source evidence explicitly says the medication was taken as directed or no missed doses were reported in a medication-adherence context. Return null when there is no usable adherence evidence.

Within each day, use medication rows where `medication_name` or `drug_name` contains escitalopram or Lexapro. Return the last non-null `medication_dose_mg` documented for escitalopram that day, in milligrams. Return null if no escitalopram dose is documented that day. This is a documented dose proxy, not proof of ingestion.

Within each day, inspect escitalopram-related `clinical_note_text`, `plan_text`, `medication_name`, `drug_name`, `medication_dose_mg`, `days_supply`, and `strength` for evidence of ongoing long-term escitalopram use or stable maintenance dosing. Rate adaptation proxy as none, short_or_uncertain, ongoing_maintenance, or long_term_maintenance. Return null if no escitalopram-use-duration or maintenance context is available in that day.
Use the `sleep_efficiency_pct` column directly from Oura sleep periods. Average values over all sleep periods assigned to the day. Higher sleep efficiency indicates less sleep/circadian disruption.

Within each day, inspect `journal_text`, `imessage_text`, `mood_labels`, and `mood_associations` for subjective stress, overwhelm, threat, uncontrollability, pressure, daily hassles, or feeling unable to cope. Rate as none, mild, moderate, or severe. Return `none` only when usable affect/stress evidence is present and indicates low or absent stress; return null if there is no usable evidence.

Within each day, inspect `calendar_summary`, `calendar_description`, `journal_text`, `imessage_text`, `transaction_name`, `merchant_name`, `finance_category_primary`, and `finance_category_detailed` for external stressful events such as conflict, deadlines, job strain, illness in self/others, bereavement, financial shock, legal/administrative problems, travel disruption, or major schedule disruption. Count distinct stressful events in the day. Return 0 if there is usable daily source evidence and no stressful event is indicated; return null if no usable event/text/transaction evidence exists.
Use the `step_count_count` column directly from Apple Health step count intervals. Sum all step counts within the day.

Count non-null `clinical_note_text` rows within each day. This measures clinical monitoring/contact volume. Return 0 when the day has rows from other sources but no clinical note; return null only if the support window has no rows at all.

Within each day, inspect `plan_text`, `clinical_note_text`, `medication_action`, `visit_type`, `department`, `calendar_summary`, and `calendar_description` for monitoring visits, follow-up plans, medication rescue, dose reinstatement, urgent care, crisis support, safety monitoring, or advice to pause/reverse taper. Return 1 if such monitoring or rescue care is documented, 0 if a relevant clinical/taper plan is present and no monitoring or rescue action is indicated, and null if there is no usable clinical or taper-care evidence.

Within each day, inspect `medication_name`, `drug_name`, `medication_dose_mg`, `medication_action`, `clinical_note_text`, `assessment_text`, and `plan_text` for non-escitalopram psychotropic medications, sleep aids, anxiolytics, stimulants, supplements, hormonal treatments, or somatic treatments that are initiated, stopped, increased, decreased, or used as needed. Count distinct non-escitalopram treatment changes or active PRN uses. Return 0 if medication/treatment evidence is present and no relevant non-escitalopram treatment is active or changed; return null if there is no usable treatment evidence.

extraction.how_to_measure: Inspect `clinical_note_text`, `assessment_text`, `journal_text`, `mood_valence`, `phq9_score`, and `gad7_score` for evidence that symptoms improved or remained well during periods without medication change, through nonpharmacologic coping, stable life conditions, or spontaneous remission. Rate as low, moderate, or high. Return null if the available evidence cannot distinguish natural recovery or resilience from medication response.

Use the `phq9_score` column directly when a PHQ-9 screening scale score is recorded. The score reflects depressive symptom burden over the prior two weeks ending at the visit date. Return null for support windows with no recorded PHQ-9 score.

Use the `gad7_score` column directly when a GAD-7 screening scale score is recorded. The score reflects anxiety symptom burden over the prior two weeks ending at the visit date. Return null for support windows with no recorded GAD-7 score.
Use the `mood_valence` column directly from Apple State of Mind entries. Average all observed entries within the day. Higher valence means better mood and therefore less internalizing symptom burden.

Within each day, inspect `local_date`, `journal_text`, `imessage_text`, `mood_labels`, and `mood_associations` for first-person evidence of depressed mood, anhedonia, anxiety, worry, irritability, panic, somatic anxiety, hopelessness, guilt, or distress. Rate severity as none, mild, moderate, or severe based only on evidence in that day. Return `none` only when there is usable mood-related text or labels and they indicate no such symptoms; return null when there is no usable symptom evidence in the support window.

Inspect `clinical_note_text`, `assessment_text`, `plan_text`, `journal_text`, medication fields, `phq9_score`, and `gad7_score` for historical improvement, relapse prevention, side effects, dose changes due to response/tolerability, or patient-reported benefit/harm while taking escitalopram. Rate net historical response/tolerability as poor_or_harmful, mixed_or_unclear, beneficial_with_side_effects, or clearly_beneficial_tolerated. Return null if no usable escitalopram response/tolerability history is available.

Use escitalopram-related `drug_name`, `medication_name`, `timestamp`, `local_date`, `days_supply`, `clinical_note_text`, and `plan_text` to estimate the length of continuous current escitalopram use before the taper decision. Prefer explicit duration statements in notes; otherwise use the span from first documented escitalopram record to the latest pre-taper escitalopram record when continuity is plausible from fills/notes. Return duration in days; return null if current-use duration cannot be estimated.

Within each day, inspect `journal_text`, `imessage_text`, `clinical_note_text`, and `plan_text` for the patient's motivation to taper or continue escitalopram, perceived benefit, side-effect concerns, dependence concerns, fear of relapse, and coping confidence. Rate taper preference as wants_continue, ambivalent, prefers_slow_taper, or wants_stop_or_fast_taper. Return null if there is no usable preference/belief evidence.

Within each day, inspect `plan_text`, `clinical_note_text`, `medication_action`, `medication_name`, and `drug_name` for the escitalopram taper plan. Classify the intended reduction speed as none_or_continue, slow_or_paused_reduction, moderate_reduction, or rapid_stop_or_large_reduction. Return null if no escitalopram taper or continuation plan is documented in the support window.

Within each day, inspect `clinical_note_text`, `plan_text`, `journal_text`, and `imessage_text` for evidence about taking escitalopram as prescribed, missed doses, extra doses, self-directed changes, or reinstatement. Rate adherence as poor, partial, or consistent. Use `consistent` only when source evidence explicitly says the medication was taken as directed or no missed doses were reported in a medication-adherence context. Return null when there is no usable adherence evidence.

Within each day, use medication rows where `medication_name` or `drug_name` contains escitalopram or Lexapro. Return the last non-null `medication_dose_mg` documented for escitalopram that day, in milligrams. Return null if no escitalopram dose is documented that day. This is a documented dose proxy, not proof of ingestion.

Within each day, inspect escitalopram-related `clinical_note_text`, `plan_text`, `medication_name`, `drug_name`, `medication_dose_mg`, `days_supply`, and `strength` for evidence of ongoing long-term escitalopram use or stable maintenance dosing. Rate adaptation proxy as none, short_or_uncertain, ongoing_maintenance, or long_term_maintenance. Return null if no escitalopram-use-duration or maintenance context is available in that day.
Use the `sleep_efficiency_pct` column directly from Oura sleep periods. Average values over all sleep periods assigned to the day. Higher sleep efficiency indicates less sleep/circadian disruption.

Within each day, inspect `journal_text`, `imessage_text`, `mood_labels`, and `mood_associations` for subjective stress, overwhelm, threat, uncontrollability, pressure, daily hassles, or feeling unable to cope. Rate as none, mild, moderate, or severe. Return `none` only when usable affect/stress evidence is present and indicates low or absent stress; return null if there is no usable evidence.

Within each day, inspect `calendar_summary`, `calendar_description`, `journal_text`, `imessage_text`, `transaction_name`, `merchant_name`, `finance_category_primary`, and `finance_category_detailed` for external stressful events such as conflict, deadlines, job strain, illness in self/others, bereavement, financial shock, legal/administrative problems, travel disruption, or major schedule disruption. Count distinct stressful events in the day. Return 0 if there is usable daily source evidence and no stressful event is indicated; return null if no usable event/text/transaction evidence exists.
Use the `step_count_count` column directly from Apple Health step count intervals. Sum all step counts within the day.

Count non-null `clinical_note_text` rows within each day. This measures clinical monitoring/contact volume. Return 0 when the day has rows from other sources but no clinical note; return null only if the support window has no rows at all.

Within each day, inspect `plan_text`, `clinical_note_text`, `medication_action`, `visit_type`, `department`, `calendar_summary`, and `calendar_description` for monitoring visits, follow-up plans, medication rescue, dose reinstatement, urgent care, crisis support, safety monitoring, or advice to pause/reverse taper. Return 1 if such monitoring or rescue care is documented, 0 if a relevant clinical/taper plan is present and no monitoring or rescue action is indicated, and null if there is no usable clinical or taper-care evidence.

Within each day, inspect `medication_name`, `drug_name`, `medication_dose_mg`, `medication_action`, `clinical_note_text`, `assessment_text`, and `plan_text` for non-escitalopram psychotropic medications, sleep aids, anxiolytics, stimulants, supplements, hormonal treatments, or somatic treatments that are initiated, stopped, increased, decreased, or used as needed. Count distinct non-escitalopram treatment changes or active PRN uses. Return 0 if medication/treatment evidence is present and no relevant non-escitalopram treatment is active or changed; return null if there is no usable treatment evidence.
